legend: Plain radiograph demonstrates a permeative tumour with patchy intramedullary sclerosis and osteolysis, and aggressive periosteal reaction best seen along the lateral cortex. There is associated cortical thickening.

diagnosis: Ewing sarcoma of the femur diaphysis
legend: Coronal T1-weighted MRI demonstrates low-signal tumour in the bone surrounded by a large T1-isointense soft tissue mass, typical for Ewing sarcoma.

diagnosis: Ewing sarcoma of the femur diaphysis
legend: The apparent diffusion coefficient map shows largely impeded diffusion with areas of less impeded diffusion centrally.

Classic Ewing sarcoma composed of uniform small round cells with round nuclei containing finely stippled chromatin and inconspicuous nucleoli, scant cytoplasm, and indistinct cytoplasmic membranes. Lighter-staining cells alternate with areas of darker, possibly apoptotic cells.

Extensive neuroectodermal differentiation (formerly called primitive neuroectodermal tumour) showing well-formed rosettes.
Atypical Ewing sarcoma with large cells.
Ewing sarcoma typically shows strong and diffuse membrane staining for CD99.

FISH analysis using a break-apart probe for the EWSR1 gene. The image shows multiple interphase nuclei stained with DAPI (blue). The FISH signals reveal one intact EWSR1 allele (red-green fusion signal) and one rearranged allele (separated red and green signals) in most cells, consistent with a heterozygous EWSR1 gene rearrangement.
source: (Figure provided by Dr. Mercedes Delgado, Virgen del Rocío University Hospital-IBiS, Sevilla)

legend: Next-generation RNA sequencing analysis of Ewing sarcoma showing in-frame fusions involving EWSR1. The upper panel demonstrates the EWSR1::FLI1 fusion transcript, while the lower panel shows the EWSR1::ERG fusion. Next-generation sequencing precisely identifies both fusion partners, offering greater specificity than EWSR1 break-apart FISH.
source: Figure provided by Dr. Juan Díaz-Martín, Virgen del Rocío University Hospital-IBiS, Sevilla

legend: The macroscopic appearance of a resected Ewing sarcoma after chemotherapy reveals a fleshy tumour with poorly defined margins, centred in the medullary canal. The tumour erodes through the cortex, forming a mass in the adjacent soft tissues.
source: Dr. Suk Wai Lam, Dept of Pathology, Leiden University Medical Center, Leiden, The Netherlands
